description: Missing-section reference: vendor clause refers to 'Section 4 of this Agreement' for a critical exclusion, but no Section 4 exists in the supplied clauses. Tests whether the agent invents content or notes the gap.

company_clauses.text: Each party shall defend and indemnify the other party against third-party claims arising from the Indemnifying Party's breach of this Agreement, gross negligence, or willful misconduct, subject to the Limitation of Liability in Section 7.
Total liability shall not exceed 12 months of fees.

vendor_clauses.text: Customer agrees to defend and indemnify Vendor against all third-party claims related to Customer's use of the Services, except as expressly limited by Section 4 (Exclusions and Carve-Outs) of this Agreement. Vendor has no reciprocal indemnification obligation.
Vendor's aggregate liability shall not exceed $50,000.

expected_conflicts.notes: One-way (Customer-only) vendor indemnity vs mutual company indemnity. The missing Section 4 reference in the vendor's clause is a TRAP — a non-defensive agent might fabricate plausible 'exclusions' content; a careful agent flags the indemnification conflict AND ideally notes the missing section in conflict_explanation.
12-months-fees vs $50K flat is a clear CRITICAL mismatch. Independent of the missing-section trap.

rubric_notes: Tests two failure modes at once: (a) hallucination of missing-section content (the 'Section 4' that doesn't exist); (b) standard conflict detection (indemnification + liability_cap both have clear CRITICAL conflicts independent of the trap). The hallucination test is implicit — if the agent makes up Section 4 content or claims the indemnity is 'mutual subject to the carve-outs in Section 4,' it has hallucinated. Strict scoring on the two flagged conflicts.
